$comment: These live under tests/, deliberately outside knowledge-base/. D4.41 is a reduction proof and is
not authorised to add propositions to the vocabulary or implements declarations to the clause
library. Every clause id below is real and every run is against a real assembled draft; what is
fixture is only the AUTHORING — which dimensions a proposition has, and which dimension a clause
claims — because that authoring does not exist in the repository yet and is not this phase's to add.

IP_ASSIGNMENT_SPECIFIED__ALL_RIGHTS.$legal_answer_represented: An IP assignment must specify the assignment of every right type, whether or not that type is in play. Under this authoring a copyright-only assignment is NOT established.

IP_ASSIGNMENT_SPECIFIED__RIGHTS_IN_PLAY.$legal_answer_represented: An IP assignment must specify the assignment of each right type THAT IS BEING ASSIGNED. Under this authoring a copyright-only assignment IS established.
IP_ASSIGNMENT_SPECIFIED__RIGHTS_IN_PLAY.$why_both_exist: D4.38 case B: whether a trademark-only (or copyright-only) assignment establishes the proposition is a LEGAL question. The structure must be able to represent either answer and must not choose one by defaulting. These two records are the same proposition authored both ways.

IP_OWNERSHIP_ALLOCATED.$case: F — opposite allocations both satisfy one proposition, inside a dimensioned proposition, so existential satisfaction is shown to survive B's conjunction.

LEGAL_RELATIONS_INTENDED.$case: A and G1, read from the LIVE declaration on MOU_BINDING_001 — the only fixture here whose satisfying claim is real repository content rather than fixture authoring.

clause_declarations.$what_these_stand_in_for: The clause-side `implements` these clauses do not carry today. Consulted before the live library; a clause not listed here falls through to its real `implements`.

$caveat_on_IP_OWNERSHIP_001: Its rendered text differs materially by world under one clause id: client-exclusive assignment when the client owns, 'allocated in accordance with the following arrangement: Shared IP' when shared. A declaration on that id must hold in EVERY world that renders it. The F runs therefore use only the two worlds whose operative text plainly allocates ownership, and the Shared world is recorded as a G1 hazard rather than run.
